edges.description: The in-frame deleted allele is transcribed and translated.
The shorter nebulin is proposed to interfere with the thin filament built with full-length nebulin.
The sarcomere lesion is expressed as distal-predominant myopathic change.

nodes.description: Reported in both patients with a mosaic deletion.

nodes.description: Myopathic change with type 1 fibre predominance, fibre atrophy and hypotrophic type 2 fibres, central nuclei, cores, and in one family nemaline bodies and cap-like structures, falling mainly on distal leg and hand muscles.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital asymmetric distal myopathy with hemifacial weakness caused by a heterozygous large de novo mosaic deletion in nebulin.
evidence.snippet: Muscle biopsies showed myopathic features with type 1 fibre predominance, strikingly hypotrophic type 2 fibres and central nuclei, but no nemaline bodies.

evidence.reference_title: Dominantly inherited distal nemaline/cap myopathy caused by a large deletion in the nebulin gene.
evidence.snippet: His first symptom was foot drop at the age of three, followed by distal muscle atrophy, slight hypomimia, high-arched palate, and weakness of the neck and elbow flexors, hands, tibialis anterior and toe extensors.

evidence.reference_title: Structural variation in nebulin and its impact on phenotype and inheritance: establishing a dominant distal phenotype caused by large deletions.

nodes.description: Nebulin normally spans the thin filament, stiffens it and is needed for normal force. The proposed lesion is a thin filament carrying an internally deleted nebulin that no longer fulfils these roles. This node is a hypothesis: no thin-filament or force measurement has been reported in muscle carrying a dominant deletion.

evidence.reference_title: Structural variation in nebulin and its impact on phenotype and inheritance: establishing a dominant distal phenotype caused by large deletions.
evidence.snippet: Nebulin stiffens the thin filament and is critical for the generation of physiological force levels

nodes.description: A single heterozygous or mosaic deletion of roughly 51 to 97 exons, always in frame and always including exons 55-77. Recessive NEB deletions are smaller (1 to 24 exons) or frameshifting, which the authors use to place the threshold for a dominant effect between 24 and 51 exons.
